quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation to keep riders together with enough space between them?

options.text: A single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while giving each rider enough space to stop safely.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent this damage.

questions.question: An engine will seize due to:

options.text: A lack of oil.
A lack of fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly. The engine overheats and stops working.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane to give the emergency vehicle space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
questions.explanation: Slow down as the dog approaches, then speed up to leave it behind.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help your balance. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent.

questions.question: If traveling with a load, the load should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to maintain balance. Attaching loads high or to a sissy bar can raise the center of gravity and affect how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should instruct them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Not talk or move unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk or move unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay still and avoid talking while riding. They should board after the engine starts and sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after completing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: How long will your license be suspended for a first DWUI offense?

options.text: 10 days.
20 days.
30 days.
90 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 90 days.
questions.explanation: Your license will be suspended for 90 days after a first DWUI offense.

questions.question: When another driver is passing you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Stay in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Staying on the right side of your lane can be dangerous. It may make the passing driver try to get back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
A windshield protects you from the wind, but goggles won't.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What should you include in your regular scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Checking your rearview mirror often.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far behind the vehicle in front of you should a motorcyclist ride?

options.text: At least two seconds.
At least three seconds.
At least four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum two-second gap behind the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions. When conditions are not perfect, increase this distance.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives you the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use?

options.text: Always ride single-file.
The formation depends on the situation.
Always ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: The formation depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight within your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your path angle may move you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your shoulders still.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your shoulders still.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can make you steer off course.

questions.question: What helps reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the seat.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow more time to stop. The passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or onto your waist or midsection, not the back of the seat.

questions.question: If you cannot see 100 feet ahead due to poor conditions, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder.
Follow another vehicle and use it as a guide.
Ride at a slightly reduced speed.
Pull over and wait until conditions improve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and wait until conditions improve.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you cannot see at least 100 feet ahead. Pull off the road and wait until visibility improves before you continue riding.

questions.question: What feeling in your steering suggests your front tire is flat?

options.text: Heavy steering.
Loose steering.
Soft steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy steering.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering is a sign your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.
